title: Exposure activation playbook (sketch) - WIP
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for an exposure activation playbook focused on cross-functional coordination for rolling out model or runtime changes. Goal is to create a compact, actionable runway for progressive exposure that teams (product, infra, SRE, monitoring, support) can use without reading 20 separate runbooks.

Scope and assumptions:
- Applies to: model upgrades, routing policy changes, tokenizer/quantization flips, and runtime config updates that can impact latency/cost/quality.
- Not in scope: UX-only feature flags (handled in product feature-flag docs) or infra-only kernel patches that are backward compatible.
- Assumes a traffic-slice orchestration layer that can route by cohort, region, and customer tier.
- Assumes telemetry: p50/p90/p99 latency, token cost, error-rate by route, model-output-quality evals, and a few product-specific KPIs.

High-level phases (activation choreography):
1) Preview & smoke (internal): 0% external, 100% internal testers + synthetic traffic. Validate basic correctness and smoke metrics.
2) Canary micro-slice: 0.1% - 1% low-risk traffic slice (non-critical customers, low-value cohorts) for 30–120m.
3) Canary extended: expand to 1% - 5% for 4–24h with automated drift checks.
4) Ramp waves: 5% -> 20% -> 50% (each wave 24–72h) with manual signoffs at each gate.
5) Full exposure: 100% or targeted permanent slice.

Roles & responsibilities (quick matrix):
- Product owner (PO): defines target user cohorts and KPI guardrails. Coordinates comms.
- Release lead (RL): owns the activation run, toggles, and gate decisions.
- Infra/SRE on-call: verifies capacity and addresses latency regressions.
- Monitoring/Observability (Obs): validates signal integrity and runs structured checks.
- Support & CS: prepared with FAQ + escalation playbook.
- Data/Quality: runs automated output-quality evals and manual review for selected prompts.

Minimum pre-activation checklist (must be green before preview):
- [ ] Canary slice configuration exists (cohort id, region, headers) and is tested in staging.
- [ ] Rollback toggle tested end-to-end (route-to-previous-model, drain behavior).
- [ ] Synthetic workload run (RPS & input distribution) shows no obvious regressions.
- [ ] Baseline snapshot for quality/latency/cost taken and stored (link to snapshot id).
- [ ] Support playbook drafted and reviewed (Slack shortcut, canned responses).
- [ ] Pager rules reviewed and temporarily tuned if necessary.
- [ ] Legal/security checklist (data residency, keys) signoff if private/deployment scope applies.

Canary metrics & automated guards (examples):
- Latency: p90 latency increase > 30% over baseline -> pause ramp and notify RL.
- Error rate: endpoint 5xx rate > 0.2% absolute increase -> immediate rollback.
- Token cost per request: > 25% increase and ROI not justified -> notify cost owner.
- Output-quality: automated eval A/B win rate < -5% (negative uplift) -> hold and triage.
- QA manual checks: 10 spot-check prompts, if >=2 show severe hallucination or catastrophic regressions -> rollback.

Automation hooks to wire in (TODOs for infra):
- webhooks from rollout orchestrator into #canary-ops channel on each gate transition.
- automated snapshot diffs pushed to a shared S3 location with pre-signed links.
- a short ‘health-evaluator’ lambda that returns PASS/WARN/FAIL and a short reason string.

Comms templates (stubs)
- Pre-launch: "Heads-up: we plan a staged activation for [change]. Preview on [date/time]. Canary start: [time]. If you see issues, ping #canary-ops and @ReleaseLead."
- Canary alert (auto): "[ALERT] Canary threshold breached: metric=[latency/p99], slice=[x], action=PAUSE. RL: @JordanP"
- Rollback note: "Rolled back [change] at [time]. Affected slice(s): [x]. Root-cause: [TBD]. Follow-up: postmort scheduled."

Gate decision rubric (quick):
- Green: no automated guards triggered, manual spot checks pass, support & SRE thumbs-up -> proceed to next wave.
- Amber: minor deviations (e.g., p90 up 15–25%), require 1-2 hour observation and additional telemetry; RL consults PO + SRE -> decide.
- Red: guard tripped (error-rate, severe latency, or quality regression) -> rollback and start incident playbook.

Rollback and recovery steps (fast path):
1) Toggle routing to previous model variant and confirm traffic shift for affected slice.
2) Disable any new feature flags tied to the change.
3) Re-open canary-only telemetry window for 60m to confirm stability.
4) Triage: collect error logs, sample requests, and eval diffs. Create Jira ticket and assign to eng on-call.

Post-activation artifacts (what to produce):
- Postmort (if amber/red) with timeline, root cause, mitigation, and action items.
- Success memo for full ramps: cost delta, latency delta, quality change, and a decision about permanent rollout.
- Model/version deprecation plan if previous variant needs to be retired.

Open questions / decisions to resolve (brain dump):
- What’s the canonical storage for snapshot baselines? (S3 path + naming convention)
- Should cost thresholds be absolute dollars or percent deltas? Mix of both could be useful.
- Who owns the final signoff at >20% exposure for enterprise customers? (RL + Account Exec?)
- How to integrate A/B statistical significance tests into automated guards (A/B platform provides p-value, but we need effect-size thresholds).
- Do we allow overlapping experiments on the same route during ramp waves? (probably not)

Immediate next steps / TODOs (owners + due):
- Maya: prototype health-evaluator endpoint and push example to github (due 2025-11-10).
- Thomas: draft support canned responses + Slack shortcuts (due 2025-11-12).
- Sofia: define 10 canonical spot-check prompts per product route and upload to Confluence (due 2025-11-14).
- Jordan: schedule cross-functional dry-run on 2025-11-17 and invite SRE, Obs, Support, Data QA.

Notes & references:
- Slack channel: #canary-ops (subscribe RL, Obs, SRE, Support)
- Example Jira: RI-2103 (routing-policy refactor), RI-2110 (monitoring adapters)
- Related confluence: "Exposure-Strategy-2025" and "Runbook-Baseline-Snapshots"

This is intentionally concise — purposefully minimal guardrails and quick decision rules so teams can run faster while preserving safety. Feedback welcome; will iterate after the dry-run and refine the automation hooks and metric thresholds.
